title: Getting started with sliR
text: sim_allometric() draws one dataset per call. compare many scenarios, build tibble parameter combinations map rows purrr::pmap() — works grid’s column names match sim_allometric()’s arguments exactly. element sims one simulated dataset one row grid. gradient (temperature, latitude, year, …) needs two extra columns whose names fixed sim_allometric(): r_grad_app r_grad_mass. gradient’s name (gradient = "Temperature") part grid, every row shares — pass separate, constant argument pmap().
code: grid <- tibble::as_tibble(expand.grid(   n = 300,   r_app_mass = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5),   b_sma = c(1 / 4, 1 / 3) )) grid #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>       n r_app_mass b_sma #>   <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl> #> 1   300        0.1 0.25  #> 2   300        0.3 0.25  #> 3   300        0.5 0.25  #> 4   300        0.1 0.333 #> 5   300        0.3 0.333 #> 6   300        0.5 0.333  set.seed(1) sims <- pmap(grid, sim_allometric) map_dbl(sims, \(d) cor(d$Append_log, d$Mass_log)) #> [1] 0.1301125 0.2919785 0.4971040 0.1032040 0.3180196 0.4958657 grad_grid <- tibble::as_tibble(expand.grid(   n = 300,   r_grad_app = c(-0.3, 0, 0.3),   r_grad_mass = -0.1 )) grad_grid #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>       n r_grad_app r_grad_mass #>   <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1   300       -0.3        -0.1 #> 2   300        0          -0.1 #> 3   300        0.3        -0.1  set.seed(1) grad_sims <- pmap(   grad_grid, sim_allometric,   gradient = "Temperature", gradient_range = c(0, 24) ) map_dbl(grad_sims, \(d) cor(d$Append_log, d$Temperature)) #> [1] -0.30254297 -0.01170966  0.29208056

what: Per-group SLI on messy real data
title: Getting started with sliR
text: Real datasets rarely every individual assigned clean group: may age-unknown, age classes may sparse — weakly allometric — per-group slope mean anything. Simulate something spirit: two age classes real mass–appendage relationship, one (juveniles) without, plus unknown-coded individuals. trusting per-group slope, check whether group’s mass appendage length actually correlated build_group_cor_tbl(). Rows coded "Unk" (default unknown_codes) excluded automatically, never appear . Age == "Juvenile" meaningful mass–appendage relationship (r near zero, large p_value), SMA slope fit group noise. calc_sli() fits slope every level present data, significance filtering , drop juveniles calling — remaining unknown-coded rows still come along, still receive sli = NA automatically. Individuals whose control value NA (, "M" birds recoded, plus original "Unk" rows included) receive sli = NA rather slope fit relationship isn’t .
code: set.seed(1) adult <- sim_allometric(n = 150, r_app_mass = 0.5, b_sma = 1 / 3) |> mutate(Age = "Adult") subadult <- sim_allometric(n = 150, r_app_mass = 0.45, b_sma = 1 / 3) |> mutate(Age = "Subadult") juvenile <- sim_allometric(n = 150, r_app_mass = 0.02, b_sma = 1 / 3) |> mutate(Age = "Juvenile") unk <- sim_allometric(n = 10) |> mutate(Age = "Unk")  birds <- bind_rows(adult, subadult, juvenile, unk) count(birds, Age) #> # A tibble: 4 × 2 #>   Age          n #>   <chr>    <int> #> 1 Adult      149 #> 2 Juvenile   150 #> 3 Subadult   148 #> 4 Unk         10 build_group_cor_tbl(birds, control = "Age") #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   Age          n  b_ols      r  p_value #>   <chr>    <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 Adult      149 0.655  0.481  5.29e-10 #> 2 Juvenile   150 0.0196 0.0147 8.58e- 1 #> 3 Subadult   148 0.528  0.393  7.88e- 7 birds |>   filter(Age != "Juvenile") |>   calc_sli(control = "Age") |>   select(Append, Mass, Age, sli) |>   filter(is.na(sli) | Age == "Adult") |>   head() #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   Append  Mass Age     sli #>    <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <dbl> #> 1   179.  82.9 Adult  177. #> 2   180.  79.5 Adult  181. #> 3   176.  78.9 Adult  177. #> 4   183.  73.5 Adult  188. #> 5   177.  71.9 Adult  183. #> 6   174.  75.0 Adult  178.

title: Standardized Length Index and Allometric Data Simulation
text: sliR computes Standardized Length Index (SLI), size correction appendage lengths, simulates allometric morphological data known scaling exponent, correlation structure, error. SLI adapts scaled mass index Peig Green (2009). index standardises mass reference length, SLI standardises length reference mass: SLIi=Ai(M0Mi)bSLI_i = A_i \left( \frac{M_0}{M_i} \right)^{b} individual ii appendage length AiA_i body mass MiM_i, arbitrary reference mass M0M_0, allometric scaling exponent bb. allometric scaling exponent calculated using standardized major axis (SMA) regression, recommended Warton et al. (2012).

Note structure: two control variables fits two models — mass interacted age, mass interacted sex — averages slopes per cell, rather fitting single age × sex interaction. keeps slope estimated marginal rather joint sample size. code: birds$Sex <- rep(c("F", "M"), length.out = nrow(birds)) birds$Age <- rep(c("Juv", "Adult"), each = 2, length.out = nrow(birds))  build_sli_slopes_tbl(birds, control = c("Age", "Sex")) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   Age   Sex       n b_sma_Age b_sma_Sex b_sli_avg #>   <chr> <chr> <int>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 Adult F       124     0.304     0.317     0.310 #> 2 Adult M       124     0.304     0.340     0.322 #> 3 Juv   F       125     0.348     0.317     0.333 #> 4 Juv   M       125     0.348     0.340     0.344 calc_sli(birds, control = c("Age", "Sex")) |>   select(Append, Mass, Age, Sex, sli) #> # A tibble: 498 × 5 #>    Append  Mass Age   Sex     sli #>     <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <chr> <dbl> #>  1   178.  82.0 Juv   F      177. #>  2   180.  78.5 Juv   M      181. #>  3   174.  76.4 Adult F      177. #>  4   185.  77.0 Adult M      188. #>  5   184.  84.5 Juv   F      181. #>  6   182.  90.3 Juv   M      174. #>  7   178.  73.0 Adult F      183. #>  8   182.  77.5 Adult M      184. #>  9   185.  84.8 Juv   F      182. #> 10   176.  75.7 Juv   M      180. #> # ℹ 488 more rows build_group_cor_tbl(birds, control = c("Age", "Sex")) #> # A tibble: 4 × 6 #>   Age   Sex       n b_ols     r    p_value #>   <chr> <chr> <int> <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1 Adult F       124 0.626 0.409 0.00000236 #> 2 Adult M       124 0.201 0.144 0.111      #> 3 Juv   F       125 0.421 0.319 0.000290   #> 4 Juv   M       125 0.434 0.352 0.0000556

title: Standardized Length Index and Allometric Data Simulation
text: sim_allometric() draws bivariate log-normal specified allometry rather raw standard deviations. allometry two degrees freedom: two correlation r_app_mass three slopes b_ols, b_sma, b_avg determine two. Supply two, none accept isometric default b_sma = 1/3, r_app_mass = 0.3. three slopes interchangeable. b_ols slope E[log⁡∣log⁡M]E[\log \mid \log M], generative slope lm() recovers. b_sma σA/σM\sigma_A / \sigma_M, slope SMA fit returns exponent calc_sli() assumes. Note clear consensus regarding line-fitting technique best allometric scaling related applications. Thus, b_avg chooses midpoint b_ols b_sma, estimator returns; convention splitting difference. implied_allometry() shows parameter set implies:
code: implied_allometry(b_sma = 1/3, r_app_mass = 0.3) #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   r_app_mass b_ols b_sma b_avg sd_log_append sd_log_mass #>        <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl> #> 1        0.3   0.1 0.333 0.217        0.0233        0.07 set.seed(3) d <- sim_allometric(n = 2000, b_sma = 1/3, r_app_mass = 0.3, trim_sd = NULL)  c(b_ols = coef(lm(Append_log ~ Mass_log, data = d))[[2]],   b_sma = coef(smatr::sma(Append_log ~ Mass_log, data = d))[["slope"]]) #>     b_ols     b_sma  #> 0.1000000 0.3333333

Omit gradient_range get z-scored gradient (mean 0, SD 1). gradient sampling design variable rather third trait, drawn uniformly default, gradient_range honoured exactly every part gradient sampled equally. gradient allometry arguments compose freely: allometry describes appendage scales mass, gradient describes responds environment. normal gradient (gradient_dist = "normal") reproduces usual three-variable multivariate normal, unbounded — happily emit latitudes beyond ±90\pm 90 — leaves extremes gradient nearly unsampled. every set correlations attainable. appendage lengthens mass falls along gradient incompatible strong positive appendage–mass correlation, sim_allometric() says rather quietly approximating. Note also correlation structure causal structure. gradient correlated traits distinguish direct effect appendage indirect one acting body size.
code: set.seed(4) gulls <- sim_allometric(   n = 2000,   # allometry: a shallower-than-isometric SMA slope, tightly correlated   b_sma = 0.28, r_app_mass = 0.6, sd_log_mass = 0.09,   # gradient: longer wings and heavier birds toward the poles   gradient = "Latitude", gradient_range = c(-90, 90),   r_grad_app = -0.3, r_grad_mass = 0.2,   trim_sd = NULL )  range(gulls$Latitude) #> [1] -89.93252  89.93252 c(r_grad_app = cor(gulls$Latitude, gulls$Append_log),   b_sma      = coef(smatr::sma(Append_log ~ Mass_log, data = gulls))[["slope"]]) #> r_grad_app      b_sma  #>      -0.30       0.28

text: Error comes two flavours, fraction trait’s standard deviation. meas_error observer error hits traits; transient_error_* genuine short-term biological fluctuation, afflicts mass far skeletal appendage. fluctuation independent appendage, attenuates observed relationship: sim_correlated() simpler raw-scale counterpart, log transform allometric target — useful building intuition fitted slope responds correlation error one trait . build_cov_mat() exposes covariance matrix sim_allometric() consumes.
code: set.seed(5) clean <- sim_correlated(n = 2000, r_app_mass = 0.3) set.seed(5) noisy <- sim_correlated(n = 2000, r_app_mass = 0.3, transient_error_mass = 1)  c(clean = cor(clean$Append, clean$Mass),   noisy = cor(noisy$Append, noisy$Mass)) #>    clean    noisy  #> 0.300000 0.196199

Rather averaging every control variable's marginal slope unconditionally, resolves one slope per cell cascade, finest coarsest, stopping first level clears minimum sample size reliable mass-appendage correlation (cor_min, cor_p_max):

title: Per-cell SMA allometric slopes, with reliability-gated fallback — build_sli_slopes_hierarchical
text: df data frame individual measurements. Append, Mass Unquoted column names appendage length body mass. default columns literally named Append Mass. columns named otherwise, pass explicitly (e.g. Append = wing, Mass = mass); informative error raised columns absent. control Character vector 0, 1, 2 grouping columns. must character factor. Level 1 (combined cell) attempted exactly two; character(0), every row resolves pooled slope. n_min_cell Minimum n level 1 (combined cell). NA wherever pass_level "none".

title: Per-cell SMA allometric slopes, with reliability-gated fallback — build_sli_slopes_hierarchical
text: cell – full cross control variables (possible, attempted, exactly two). Gated n_min_cell. Single-variable marginals – control variable's slope, pooling across . Gated n_min_marginal; averaged together pass, used unblended one . pooled slope – fit every row df, regardless control. Reached finer level passes, used every cell control empty. df's pooled mass-appendage correlation gates whole cascade: reliable, every cell's slope NA (pass_level = "none") rather falling back unreliable pooled fit. keeps caller's downstream SLI defined either df's rows none, matching shared-N convention body-size-correction methods need fair comparison across . Unlike build_sli_slopes_tbl() build_group_cor_tbl(), rows whose control values NA match unknown_codes dropped: collapsed explicit "Unk" class per variable, cascades three levels every class – special case automatic fallback pooled.

title: Standardized Length Index (SLI) — calc_sli
text: Size-corrects appendage length rescaling every individual common reference body mass, following scaled mass index Peig & Green (2009). Whereas index standardises mass reference length, SLI standardises length reference mass:

title: Standardized Length Index (SLI) — calc_sli
code: calc_sli(   df,   Append = Append,   Mass = Mass,   b_sli = 0.33,   M0 = NULL,   control = NULL,   method = c("average", "hierarchical"),   unknown_codes = c("Unk", "U", "Unknown"),   slope_diff_warn = 0.15,   n_min_cell = 50,   n_min_marginal = 100,   cor_min = 0.3,   cor_p_max = 0.05,   rename_col = NULL,   sort = FALSE )

title: Standardized Length Index (SLI) — calc_sli
text: df data frame individual measurements. Append, Mass Unquoted column names appendage length body mass. default columns literally named Append Mass. columns named otherwise, pass explicitly (e.g. Append = wing, Mass = mass); informative error raised columns absent. b_sli Scalar allometric scaling exponent. default 0.33 (\(\approx 1/3\)) assumes isometry, linear dimensions scale cube root mass. Ignored control supplied. Set empirically estimated SMA slope relax isometry. M0 Reference mass individuals standardised. NULL (default) uses mean Mass. \(M_0\) arbitrary scalar: rescales every SLI value constant factor changes units index, never ranking individuals result subsequent location-invariant analysis. title: Standardized Length Index (SLI) — calc_sli
text: $$SLI_i = A_i \left( \frac{M_0}{M_i} \right)^{b}$$ \(A_i\) \(M_i\) individual \(\)'s appendage length body mass, \(M_0\) arbitrary reference mass, \(b\) allometric scaling exponent relating length mass.

title: Standardized Length Index (SLI) — calc_sli

text: Changes prompted first real use package, migrating SLI-allens-rule manuscript’s simulation analysis onto sliR. Added “Getting started” vignette (vignette("sliR")) covering two workflows shown README: simulating across parameter grid (including gradient case), computing SLI per group messy real data unknown-coded weakly-allometric groups. Added sim_grid(), thin wrapper maps [sim_allometric()] data frame parameter combinations row-binds result, stamping .scenario column identifying row produced simulated dataset. sim_correlated()’s r argument renamed r_app_mass, matching sim_allometric()’s name quantity. r still works warns per session; removed future version. inst/CITATION now bakes package version title, just note field: common CSL styles (APA, Elsevier-Harvard, Nature, Vancouver checked) drop note Manual entry, silently lost version number reproducibility depends . Set pkgdown site (_pkgdown.yml, .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml) reference vignette render browsable site, deployed gh-pages push. build_cov_mat() gains sd_gradient argument (default 1). Previously gradient always entered unit standard deviation, returned matrix standardised structure rather covariance caller’s actual system; user rescale gradient block hand. default unchanged, existing calls unaffected. ?sim_allometric now documents two behaviours surprised first user porting existing code: (1) functions consume random-number stream, internal draw order implementation detail, exact reproducibility tied pinned package version; (2) outlier trimming applied jointly appendage mass, sequentially, retained sample can differ slightly code trims one trait .

title: sliR 0.1.0
text: First release. calc_sli() computes Standardized Length Index, adapting scaled mass index Peig & Green (2009) standardise appendage length reference mass. Supports scalar exponent per-group SMA slopes via control. build_sli_slopes_tbl() build_group_cor_tbl() fit diagnose per-group allometric slopes. implied_allometry() resolves full allometry sufficient subset parameters (correlation OLS, SMA, midpoint slopes). sim_allometric() simulates log-normal morphology target allometry, optionally along environmental gradient drawn bounded, evenly-sampled design variable. sim_correlated() build_cov_mat() provide raw-scale bivariate draw underlying covariance matrix.
